title: Development of Surgical and Visualization Procedures to Analyze Vasculatures by Mouse Tail Edema Model
author: Kumegawa, Yamada, et al.
materials: Flexible and solid as surgical material

Tissue samples were fixed in 4% (wt/vol) PFA overnight, dehydrated in methanol (25–100%) washes and embedded in paraffin. The paraffin blocks were sectioned serially (10 μm thick) with a microtome (902,100, HM325, PHC, Japan), placed on slides, deparaffinized and rehydrated. Antigen retrieval was performed with either by citrate buffer or by autoclaving at 121 °C, 1 min. For primary antibody staining, the following antibodies were utilized: anti-CD31 (endothelial markers; 1/200, AF3628, goat, R&D systems) and anti-LYVE1 (L.V. endothelial marker; 1/100, ab14917, rabbit, Abcam). For secondary antibody reaction, the following antibody was utilized: Invitrogen Donkey anti-goat IgG Alexa Fluor 488 (1/200, Thermo Fisher Scientific). Total number of 533 serial section of fluorescent immunostaining images were incorporated as digital data and processed by Amira software to construct 3D images of edema and its adjacent regions (Fig. 4).

steps.title: Prepare silicone sheet and suture
steps.instruction: Obtain a 0.5 mm thin transparent silicone sheet (Tigers Polymer, Osaka, Japan) and 7‑0 nylon suture; cut the sheet to fit a 5 mm × 5 mm square area of the mouse tail.

steps.title: Insert and suture sheet into tail
steps.instruction: Under anesthesia, create a 5 mm square incision at the desired tail site, carefully insert the silicone sheet into the wound, and secure it with 7‑0 nylon sutures.

steps.title: Harvest tail tissue for analysis
steps.instruction: At the chosen post‑operative time point, excise the tail segment containing the operated area, taking a 5 mm central piece and a 10 mm peripheral piece relative to the surgical site.

steps.title: Fix tissue overnight in PFA
steps.instruction: Immerse the harvested tail pieces in 4 % (wt/vol) paraformaldehyde (PFA) prepared in phosphate‑buffered saline (PBS) and fix overnight at room temperature (~25 °C).

steps.title: Wash samples in PBS
steps.instruction: Rinse the fixed tails with PBS and incubate them in fresh PBS overnight at ~25 °C with gentle shaking.

steps.title: Clear tissue with CUBIC‑L
steps.instruction: Perform CUBIC‑L clearing in two stages:

substeps.instruction: Incubate samples in a 1:1 mixture of CUBIC‑L solution (T3740, Tokyo Kasei Kogyo) and PBS for 1 day at 37 °C with gentle shaking.
Transfer samples to 100 % CUBIC‑L solution and shake at 37 °C for an additional 2 days.

steps.title: Wash samples post‑CUBIC‑L
steps.instruction: Rinse the cleared tissues in PBS overnight at room temperature (~25 °C) with gentle shaking.

steps.title: Clear tissue with CUBIC‑R
steps.instruction: Perform CUBIC‑R clearing in two stages:

substeps.instruction: Incubate samples in a 1:1 mixture of CUBIC‑R solution (T3741, Tokyo Chemical Industry) and PBS for 1 day at room temperature with gentle shaking.
Transfer samples to 100 % CUBIC‑R solution and shake at room temperature for a further 2 days.

steps.title: Dehydrate and embed in paraffin
steps.instruction: Dehydrate the cleared tails through a graded methanol series (25 % → 100 % methanol) and embed the tissue in paraffin blocks.

steps.title: Section paraffin blocks at 10 µm
steps.instruction: Using a microtome (e.g., model 902,100, HM325, PHC, Japan), cut serial sections 10 µm thick and mount them on glass slides.

steps.title: Deparaffinize and rehydrate slides
steps.instruction: Remove paraffin from the sections with xylene (or equivalent) and rehydrate through descending ethanol series to water.

steps.title: Apply primary antibodies
steps.instruction: Incubate slides with the following primary antibodies diluted in appropriate buffer:

substeps.instruction: Anti‑CD31 (goat, R&D Systems, catalog AF3628) at 1 : 200 dilution.
Anti‑LYVE1 (rabbit, Abcam, catalog ab14917) at 1 : 100 dilution.

steps.title: Apply secondary antibody
steps.instruction: After washing, incubate slides with Invitrogen Donkey anti‑goat IgG Alexa Fluor 488 (Thermo Fisher Scientific) at 1 : 200 dilution.

steps.title: Inject FITC‑dextran for vascular labeling
steps.instruction: Immediately before imaging, inject FITC‑dextran (green fluorescent tracer) intravenously to label functional lymphatic and blood vessels.

steps.title: Capture fluorescence video
steps.instruction: Observe the tail under a fluorescence microscope, record video at 60 i 17 M (FH) resolution, 1920 × 1080 pixels, 30 frames / s, with an average bitrate of 17 Mbps; extract still snapshots as needed.

steps.title: Acquire serial images
steps.instruction: Collect a total of 533 serial fluorescent images (CD31 or LYVE1 stained) covering the entire region of interest.

steps.title: Reconstruct 3D volume in Amira
steps.instruction: Import the 533 image series into Amira software and generate a three‑dimensional reconstruction of the edema and adjacent vasculature.
